claims.text: The starting catalyst is a multi-element automotive alloy with nearly equiatomic principal elements and low platinum-group-metal content.
A 700–900 °C reductive pretreatment will cause selective migration of active transition-metal elements to the catalyst surface.
The reductive pretreatment will produce segregated active transition-metal clusters.
The reductive pretreatment will form a robust intermetallic surface or interface.
The restructured surface will contain oxygen-buffering sites.
The restructured intermetallic surface or interface will enhance oxygen mobility and oxygen-buffering capacity.
The restructured surface layer will resist sintering.
The restructured surface layer will resist oxidation.
The pretreatment-induced structural change will improve resistance to thermal aging.
The pretreatment-induced structural change will improve resistance to poisoning by H2O and NO.
The untreated catalyst suffers activity loss and structural degradation, including sintering and oxidation, under the specified exhaust conditions.
Relative to the untreated catalyst, the pretreated catalyst will exhibit a higher sustained turnover frequency.
Relative to the untreated catalyst, the pretreated catalyst will exhibit better structural stability and less performance degradation over time.
The activity and durability improvements can be achieved without increasing platinum-group-metal usage.
The proposed benefits are expected under transient, low-temperature exhaust conditions with moderate H2O and NO loadings.
Conditions more extreme than the stated operating envelope may not provide the same improvements.
